statusLegend.done: Implemented AND covered by an automated check that passes
statusLegend.partial: Implemented in part; the gap is stated in `notes`
statusLegend.blocked: Cannot proceed without something only the user can supply
statusLegend.deferred: Explicitly out of scope for now by agreement

requirements.title: K-8 curriculum split into Core and Advanced/Extended topics
requirements.notes: Transcribed from Appendix A with core/adv track flags on every unit.

requirements.title: Grades K-2 cover number sense, patterns, early logic, intro combinatorics
requirements.notes: K-2 authored: counting, counting back, adding/subtracting within 10 and 20, even/odd, flat shapes, tens and ones, arrays, place value to 1000, subtracting within 20, the equal sign, word problems, comparing two-digit numbers, measuring length, fluency within 20, adding/subtracting within 1000, money, equal groups, rulers, time to five minutes, adding/subtracting within 100, comparing three-digit numbers, mental math with 10s/100s, estimating length, line plots, polygons by attribute, rows & columns, halves/thirds/fourths, commutative/associative properties, ten more/ten less, telling time, bar & picture graphs, defining attributes, composing shapes, halves & fourths, composing/decomposing numbers, solid shapes, combining shapes, comparing size/weight, sorting, and picture graphs. All Grade 1 and Grade 2 core (non-advanced) topics are now authored, and Kindergarten core is authored except ordinal numbers, repeating patterns and logic puzzles -- none of which have a real CCSSM standard (like g1-coins, deliberately skipped rather than guessed). 43 of the 80 K-2 topics now have questions; Grade K and Grade 1 advanced/enrichment topics still do not.

requirements.title: Grades 3-5 cover fluency, fractions, decimals, geometry + prime factorisation, modular arithmetic, probability
requirements.notes: Grade 3 authored: multiplication, division, fractions as numbers, comparing fractions, equivalent fractions, whole numbers as fractions, area, perimeter, rounding, time to the minute, classifying quadrilaterals, properties of multiplication, two-step word problems, arithmetic patterns, adding/subtracting within 1000, multiplying by multiples of ten. Grade 4 authored: multiplicative comparison, multi-step word problems, factors/primes/composites, multi-digit multiplication, division with remainders, place value to a million, adding/subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, decimal notation, comparing decimals, area/perimeter formulas, lines/rays/angles, classifying figures, symmetry, number/shape patterns, multiplying fractions by whole numbers, units of measure, line plots with fractions, measuring angles. Grade 5 authored: numerical expressions, decimal operations, unlike denominators, place value to thousandths, multiplying fractions, dividing with unit fractions, converting units, patterns/ordered pairs, two-digit divisors, fraction word problems, line plots with fractions, volume, the coordinate plane, classifying figures by hierarchy. All Grade 3, 4 AND 5 core (non-advanced) topics are now authored. 49 of the 114 grade 3-5 topics now have questions; prime factorisation, modular arithmetic and probability topics are not yet among them.

requirements.title: Grades 6-8 cover ratios, algebra, geometry, statistics + full modular arithmetic, quadratics, graph theory, proof
requirements.notes: Map covers ratios, algebra, geometry, statistics plus modular arithmetic, quadratics, graph theory and proof for 6-8. Grade 6 authored: coordinate plane, ratios, percent, unit conversion, decimal operations, exponents, one-variable equations, dividing fractions, equivalent expressions, dependent/independent variables, area of polygons, volume with fractional edges, polygons on the coordinate plane, nets & surface area, statistical questions, center & variability, data displays -- all of Grade 6 core (non-advanced) is now authored. Grade 7 authored: unit rates with fractions, proportional relationships, operations with rational numbers, markups/discounts/interest, terminating/repeating decimals, expanding & factoring, multi-step problems, equations & inequalities, scale drawings, constructing figures, circles, angle relationships, volume & surface area, random sampling, probability models, compound events -- all of Grade 7 core (non-advanced) is now authored. Grade 8 authored: irrational numbers, radicals and integer exponents, linear equations. 36 of the 134 grade 6-8 topics now have questions.

requirements.title: Comic lessons with sequential panels and interactive elements
requirements.notes: 3 lessons (arrays, fractions, ratios) as short panel sequences with a speaking monster and inline checks, illustrated with simple original SVG diagrams. Wrong answers on a check never block progress -- this teaches, it does not gate. Progress saves after every panel and resumes correctly. Only 3 of 328 topics have a lesson; most content still starts directly at practice.

requirements.title: Practice problems: varied types, immediate feedback, hints, full solutions
requirements.notes: Five question types (plus the new plot-input type) authored and graded server-side, now exercised across 49 topics and all 9 grade levels. Dynamic geometry beyond point-plotting still missing.

requirements.title: Algorithmically generated problem variants
requirements.notes: Seeded templates for five topics give unlimited fresh variants. The seed travels in the question id, so the server can rebuild and mark the exact problem later without storing it — which also means a review item shows the identical question. Grading, hints and error analysis all work unchanged on generated questions.

requirements.title: Open-ended puzzles with multiple solution paths
requirements.notes: 8 open-ended puzzles across four difficulties, sitting outside the adaptive path. Hints come one at a time and a wrong answer never reveals the solution, which is what keeps a puzzle worth returning to. Multiple valid solution PATHS are encouraged by the prompts, but the checker accepts a final value rather than reasoning.

requirements.title: Proof exercises (drag-drop blocks, fill-in, free-form)
requirements.notes: Ordering, fill-in-the-reason and missing-step exercises implemented. Free-form proof entry is not built - it would need real symbolic or AI validation, and I will not claim structural checking is the same thing.

requirements.title: Explainer videos with captions and speed control
requirements.notes: Requires video production; no assets exist.

requirements.title: Interactive simulations and dynamic geometry
Assessments: diagnostic, formative, summative
requirements.notes: All three kinds reachable: adaptive diagnostic, formative practice with immediate feedback and explanation, and summative mastery check with a pass mark.

requirements.title: Text-to-speech read-aloud with text highlighting
requirements.notes: Browser speech synthesis with maths spoken as words rather than symbols (times, divided by, half, quarter, the point 3 comma -2, the absolute value of -7), and now word-by-word highlighting while it reads (check:read-aloud-highlight). The difficulty is that the spoken string is not the written one -- '4 x 6' is spoken '4 times 6' -- so the browser's boundary character index points into a string that has already drifted from what is on screen, and highlighting on it underlines the wrong word, further wrong with every transformation. Each rewrite rule now records the written range it consumed against the spoken range it produced, so a position in the speech resolves back to the exact written text. A rewritten expression stays highlighted whole while it is said, since underlining just the '4' while the voice says 'times' is worse than no highlight. The highlight is an addition and never a requirement: where the boundary event does not fire the text simply reads normally. Marked with an underline as well as a background so it does not depend on colour, cleared when speech stops and when the question changes, and the spoken output is pinned unchanged across ten maths phrases so highlighting cannot alter what a child hears.

requirements.title: Productive struggle: attempts before hints; first hint never gives the solution
Mastery-based progression: 90% core, 80% advanced
requirements.notes: Server decides the threshold from the topic's track (core 90, adv 80) and returns it with each run; client no longer guesses.

requirements.title: Spaced review adapting to individual forgetting curves
requirements.notes: SM-2 style scheduler per (learner, topic): interval grows by an ease factor on success and collapses to one day on a lapse, with ease floored at 1.3. Every run, adaptive session and mastery check updates it.

requirements.title: Proof and justification progression K-8
requirements.notes: Progression exists: choosing a supporting reason at grade 1, ordering an argument at grade 3, two-column style with reasons at grade 5, contradiction at grade 6, induction at grade 8. Only five proofs authored so far.

requirements.title: Competition readiness: Contest Corner with past problems and drills
requirements.notes: Timed contest formats exist. No Contest Corner UI or strategy guides yet.

requirements.title: Number theory track
requirements.notes: Number theory topics mapped K-8 (k-evenodd through g8-rsa). No questions authored.

requirements.title: Combinatorics track
requirements.notes: Combinatorics topics mapped K-8 (k-combos through g8-designs). No questions authored.

requirements.title: Algebra extensions
requirements.notes: Algebra extension topics mapped G2-G8. No questions authored.

requirements.title: Geometry extensions
requirements.notes: Geometry extension topics mapped G2-G8. No questions authored.

requirements.title: Probability and statistics extensions
requirements.notes: Probability/statistics extension topics mapped G4-G8. No questions authored.

requirements.title: Proof techniques track
requirements.notes: Direct proof, proof by contradiction (infinitude of primes) and induction (sum formula) are represented. Pigeonhole and extremal principle are not.

requirements.title: Content authored/reviewed by educators with competition experience
requirements.notes: Process requirement about people, not code. Needs the user to define a review workflow and reviewers.

requirements.title: Reviewed for diversity, inclusivity, absence of stereotypes
requirements.notes: Automated scan for the crude, common failure modes: gendered activity stereotypes and a suspiciously narrow cast of names. Verified to fire on deliberately stereotyped text and stay silent on neutral content. All 198 authored questions manually reviewed and scan clean, with a cast of 8 named characters across genders. This is a first-pass tool, not a substitute for human editorial review, and says so in its own comment - pattern matching cannot judge nuance or catch subtler bias.

requirements.title: WCAG 2.1 AA accessible content incl. alt text and captions
requirements.notes: UI meets WCAG 2.1 AA (check:accessibility-wcag-aa), images and SVGs carry text alternatives, and questions can be read aloud. Video captions and alt text for authored lesson art are not applicable yet - no such content exists.

requirements.title: Math notation via LaTeX with MathML accessibility
requirements.notes: Arithmetic, fractions, absolute value, coordinates, ratios and exponents render as MathML with an aria-label giving the spoken form, so assistive technology announces mathematics rather than punctuation. Negative numbers use a true minus sign. Unrecognised text is returned as escaped plain text rather than wrapped in markup that would misrepresent it. LaTeX input for authors is not supported - MathML was chosen because it needs no client library and is what assistive technology consumes.

requirements.title: Content versioned and approved through CMS workflow
requirements.notes: Content is versioned in the repository, so every change already has an author, a diff and a history; the missing half -- a record that a human reviewed a specific version, and a way to see what a child sees -- is now built (check:content-review-workflow). Approvals are bound to a hash of the exact content and are revoked automatically by any change of meaning, with the superseded record kept rather than overwritten, since who approved what and when is the point of having a workflow. Approve and request-changes are distinct outcomes, both carrying reviewer notes, and an estate-wide view reports how much content is approved, never reviewed, or edited since sign-off. Editorial authority is admin-only. A separate hosted CMS is deliberately not built: the content lives in the repository, and moving it into a database would trade real version control for a worse copy of it.

requirements.title: Onboarding: grade selection or diagnostic assessment with skill map
requirements.notes: Adaptive diagnostic held server-side: difficulty steps up after two correct, down after two wrong. Produces a per-section skill map and a placement recommendation, stored against the learner and retrievable. Verified that strong and weak learners place differently.

requirements.title: Dashboard: dual-track map, avatar, daily goals, streaks, challenge of the day
requirements.notes: Dashboard covers grade/topic/tier navigation with placement and mastery entry points, the dual-track map, avatar with earned accessories, streaks, daily goals and a challenge of the day (check:avatar-and-daily). The challenge is derived from the calendar date rather than drawn at random or stored: everyone gets the SAME problem on a given day, which is what makes it something to talk about at a table or in class, and it cannot be re-rolled by reloading until an easy one comes up. One attempt per learner per day, and the question is not served again afterwards so the explanation cannot be farmed for a retry. Daily targets are derived from the stored weekly goal rather than kept separately, so the two cannot disagree, and rounded UP -- rounding three rounds a week down to zero a day would present a real goal as no goal at all.

requirements.title: Lesson player with comic panels, narration, embedded checks, resume
requirements.notes: Lesson player with narration (read-aloud on every panel), embedded checks, and resume-where-you-left-off, verified panel by panel. Progress saving on exit and picking up mid-lesson both confirmed rather than assumed.

requirements.title: Practice mode: adaptive sequence, 3-level hints, feedback, stars, mistake review
requirements.notes: Adaptive session held server-side: difficulty follows performance, three-level hints reduce the star award, and every mistake is returned at the end with its answer and explanation. Time on task recorded.

requirements.title: Puzzle area with trophies and elegant-solution badges
requirements.notes: Puzzle area with untimed play, per-puzzle hints, gold/silver/bronze trophies reflecting how many hints were taken, and an Elegant Solution badge for solving unaided. Points scale with difficulty and are awarded once.

requirements.title: Mastery checks: no hints, configurable threshold, retake
requirements.notes: Server-issued check drawn across all tiers, marked server-side, hints refused with 409 while live, replay blocked, recorded under its own 'mastery' tier. Retake is allowed and counted.

requirements.title: Review and remediation driven by spaced repetition
requirements.notes: Review endpoint merges unmastered topics with those the spacing schedule says are due, each labelled with a reason. No dedicated review UI yet.

requirements.title: Social: moderated leaderboards, clans, no direct messaging
requirements.notes: Leaderboards are OFF by default and only a teacher can enable them, per class. Anonymised unless the teacher allows names, though a parent always sees their own child labelled. No global board and no messaging of any kind. Clans and team challenges are not built.

requirements.title: Competition prep mode: timed sets, mock contests, analytics
requirements.notes: Timed papers in five formats (Kangaroo, MOEMS, AMC 8, MATHCOUNTS, quick drill), scored server-side with the deadline owned by the server: a late submission is still marked but scores zero. Per-format history and topic breakdown recorded. NOT done: percentile ranking against other students, leaderboards, and a curated archive of real contest problems (licensing is blocked, 10.9).

requirements.title: Proof trainer with validation and template library
requirements.notes: Proof trainer with three exercise kinds (order the steps, match each step to its reason, supply the missing step) across grades 1 to 8. Checking is structural and honest about it: an ordering proof is right when the steps are in a valid order, a reasons proof when each step is paired with a justification that supports it. Feedback names which steps are wrong without revealing the answer. NOT done: free-form proof entry with validation, and the template library.

requirements.title: AI tutor: chat hints, misconception detection, safety filters
requirements.notes: Needs an LLM provider account, API key and a billing decision from the user.

requirements.title: Create and manage multiple child accounts
Set curriculum track per child (Core/Enrichment/Competition)
requirements.notes: Core, enrichment and competition, stored per learner and settable at creation or later. The setting decides which units the child's curriculum endpoint returns — core learners are not shown advanced material at all — so it changes what they are offered rather than labelling the record. An unrecognised track is refused rather than coerced to core.

requirements.title: Progress monitoring: level, mastery, time spent, readiness
requirements.notes: Level, mastery and run history were already recorded. Added server-measured time on task for every round (sessions carry startedAt; client-reported durations are clamped so a tab left open overnight is not eight hours of study), aggregated by topic and by day. Rounds predating the column store NULL and are reported as unmeasured rather than as zero, which would have understated every average. Competition readiness is five separate signals with the evidence behind each and a named next step, not one number.

requirements.title: Weekly email summary
requirements.notes: Needs an SMTP provider and credentials from the user.

requirements.title: Alerts when struggling, inactive, or ready to advance
requirements.notes: Error categories and the review queue give the raw signal for struggling. No alerting or notification yet (needs the blocked email/push provider).

requirements.title: Goal setting with notifications
requirements.notes: Parents set a weekly rounds target per learner; progress is computed from runs actually recorded in the last seven days, with met and at-risk flags. Notifications when a goal is met or at risk need the blocked email/push provider (9.4).

requirements.title: Curriculum overview with sample problems
requirements.notes: Per-topic overview with a real sample problem, verified to never leak its answer, reachable without signing in so a parent can look before committing. Shows the standard it maps to when one exists.

requirements.title: Class management and rostering import
requirements.notes: Teachers hold a role; classes have join codes and the PARENT adds their own learner, so a teacher can never pull in a child unilaterally. LMS/rostering import (Clever, ClassLink, Google Classroom) is blocked on vendor accounts (9.1).

requirements.title: Assignment tools with due dates and per-group tracks
requirements.notes: Assignments per class with optional tier and due date, validated against real topics, plus per-group differentiation and individual accommodations (check:differentiated-assignments). Groups let a teacher set different work for part of a class without creating a second class and splitting the register; a group assignment reaches its members and nobody else. Accommodations adjust one learner's tier and deadline on one assignment, recorded against the assignment rather than as a duplicate so the teacher keeps one thing to track. The child's list and the teacher's view are built from the same rows and the adjustment is disclosed to the learner alongside the class deadline -- an extension the child cannot see is worth nothing to the person it was granted for. Only learners already in the class can be grouped or accommodated, so neither route can reach a child the teacher has no relationship with.

requirements.title: Class progress dashboard and standards heatmap
requirements.notes: Class dashboard shows every learner against every assignment with best score and mastery, plus a per-topic heatmap of attempts, average and mastery counts. Cross-teacher and parent access both refused.

requirements.title: Reporting: PDF/CSV export incl. gifted report
requirements.notes: Learner and class CSV exports plus a printable HTML report the browser turns into a PDF, which keeps a PDF engine out of the dependency tree. A dedicated gifted-and-talented report is not built.

requirements.title: Competition team management
requirements.notes: Competition teams within a class (check:competition-teams), managed by the class teacher because team selection is a decision about children that belongs to an adult who knows them. A learner belongs to at most one team, enforced by the schema rather than by remembering to check: two teams sharing a member would count that child's paper twice and rank both squads on work only one of them did. Only learners already in the class can be entered. Standings use each member's BEST paper and publish the sum, the average AND the squad size together -- a sum rewards the bigger team and an average rewards the smaller one, so publishing only one hides whichever unfairness it carries behind a figure a teacher cannot interrogate. Names follow the same anonymisation setting as every other board here, with a parent always able to see their own child.

requirements.title: School/district management
requirements.notes: Admin role granted out of band via ADMIN_EMAILS, never self-assignable at signup (verified). Platform-wide counts and role breakdown. Multi-school and multi-district hierarchy is not modelled.

requirements.title: Usage and performance analytics
requirements.notes: Aggregate analytics: user and learner counts, active learners in the last seven days, attainment distribution across four bands, and the ten hardest topics by average score. Verified to contain no learner name or parent email — administrators see shape, not individual children's work.

requirements.title: Compliance: retention policies and audit logs
requirements.notes: Retention policy published with live counts, audit log readable by admins, and admin access to the audit log is itself audited (verified). Automated deletion on a retention schedule is not built; erasure is self-service and immediate.

requirements.title: Points, with advanced content worth more
requirements.notes: Points awarded on every finished round, weighted higher for advanced topics as the spec requires, and reduced by hint use without ever going negative.

requirements.title: 100+ badges incl. subject and meta badges
requirements.notes: 108 badges across 14 groups including subject, breadth and meta badges (check:badge-catalogue). Each badge carries the condition that earns it in the same object as its name and hint, which is the design decision rather than tidiness: with award conditions scattered through the request handlers the catalogue and the code drift, and both failures hurt a child -- a catalogued badge nothing can award is a promise that never arrives, and a badge awarded by code but missing from the catalogue renders to them as a raw string like 'streak_30'. Awards are issued by walking the catalogue, so nothing outside it is awardable and every entry is reachable by construction; the check asserts both directions. Conditions are evaluated against a snapshot of the learner's record rather than fired from single events, so a badge added later is earned retroactively by whoever already qualifies. Six badges describe a moment rather than a state (a round finished without hints, a puzzle solved cold) and are awarded at the event, but are still named in the one catalogue. Awarded once, enforced by a unique index.

requirements.title: Avatar customisation tied to achievements
requirements.notes: Three original monsters with four moods, chosen per learner and shown throughout, plus twelve unlockable accessories across six slots earned by holding a badge (check:avatar-and-daily). Unlocked by achievement rather than priced in points, deliberately: points accumulate with time spent, so a points shop rewards whoever sat there longest and the child grinding easy rounds ends up the most decorated. A badge is earned for doing a specific thing, so what a learner wears says what they actually did. Locked items are shown with the badge that unlocks them named -- hiding them would make the collection invisible until it was already complete. Equipping an unearned item is refused server-side, which is an authorisation check rather than a presentation detail: without it a learner could wear the contest sash by posting its id and every badge on display would stop meaning anything. One item per slot.

requirements.title: Levels and prestige for advanced tracks
requirements.notes: Overall level derived from points on a square-root curve, plus per-subject levels and prestige on the advanced track (check:levels-and-prestige). Points are attributed to the track the work was done on, so core work cannot raise an advanced standing -- pooled, a child would be told their competition level went up because they did their times tables. Prestige is DERIVED from the advanced level rather than stored as a counter: a stored counter and a computed level are two records of one fact and they drift, and a child seeing their stars disagree with their level has no way to tell which is right. Core has levels but no prestige, as the spec asks -- the advanced track is where the ceiling is worth passing more than once. The awards.track column is nullable because rows written before it existed were never attributed, and calling them core would invent a measurement.

requirements.title: Streaks with freezes
requirements.notes: Daily streak counted from activity, breaking when a day is skipped, with 3-day and 7-day badges, plus streak freezes (check:streak-freezes). A freeze is earned by a full week of unbroken practice and spent on ONE missed day, at the moment of the next activity, and is recorded against the specific day it covered. Two constraints make it honest rather than decorative: a freeze cannot be applied retroactively, so a learner returning after a fortnight has a broken streak and is told so -- otherwise one token repairs a month and the number stops meaning anything -- and the balance is capped at two, because an uncapped balance turns a hard month into an unbreakable streak that no longer reports practice at all. A frozen day protects the run without being counted as a day of practice. Spent freezes are consumed and cannot cover a second gap.

requirements.title: Narrative arc with student-influenced outcomes
requirements.notes: Monsters react to answers, which is character but not narrative. No story arc.

requirements.title: Unlockable content and hidden areas
requirements.notes: Unlockable content is built as the avatar wardrobe (check:avatar-and-daily): twelve accessories gated behind specific badges, visible while locked with their requirement named, and refused server-side until earned. Hidden AREAS of the curriculum are deliberately not built -- gating maths content behind achievement would withhold teaching from the children who most need it, which is the opposite of what this product is for. Cosmetic unlocks carry the reward without that cost.

requirements.title: Leaderboards, tournaments, clans
requirements.notes: Class leaderboards with teacher control and anonymisation. School-wide and global boards are deliberately not built - they would rank a child against strangers. Weekly tournaments and clan challenges are not implemented.

requirements.title: Mini-games reinforcing concepts
Achievement titles for advanced mastery
requirements.notes: Six titles earned by combinations of badges - Grand Combinatorialist, Master of Modular Arithmetic, Proof-Wright, Contest Contender, Steady Hand, Apprentice - ordered strongest first so the displayed title is the best held. Every title's requirements are validated against real badges.

requirements.title: Adaptive diagnostic using IRT/BKT producing a skill map
requirements.notes: Three-parameter logistic IRT (app/server/src/irt.js) drives the diagnostic: ability is re-estimated after every answer, the next question is the one carrying most information at that ability, and placement follows the measured ability rather than the raw percentage. Guessing is discounted per question type, so a correct four-option answer counts for less than a correct free-input one. Estimation is expected-a-posteriori rather than maximum likelihood, which diverges on the all-correct and all-wrong patterns that a 12-question diagnostic produces routinely. BKT tracks per-skill knowledge (check:knowledge-tracing) and the skill map is produced and stored. Remaining refinement, not a gap in the requirement: item difficulty and discrimination are cold-start priors taken from the authored tier, not fitted from real response data — fitting them needs the learner corpus that 13.2 is blocked on.

requirements.title: Knowledge graph of prerequisite skills incl. advanced nodes
requirements.notes: 459 authored edges across 315 topics, acyclic, 239 of them crossing grades. Includes the dependencies the spec names (modular arithmetic requires division with remainders; combinatorics requires the multiplication principle). Exposed via /api/topics/:id/prereqs and a /next endpoint that separates what a learner is ready for from what is blocked, naming the missing prerequisites.

requirements.title: BKT/DKT mastery updates and bandit difficulty selection
requirements.notes: Bayesian Knowledge Tracing implemented and verified: P(known) updated per answer with slip and guess terms, guess rate scaled to the number of options, and mastery requiring both confidence and enough observations so a lucky answer cannot declare it. Difficulty selection is now a Thompson-sampling bandit over the three tiers (check:bandit-difficulty), rewarded by correctness WEIGHTED BY DIFFICULTY — a correctness-only reward converges on the easiest tier and parks the learner there, which is the opposite of adaptive. The two-in-a-row streak rule it replaced is gone. NOT done: Deep Knowledge Tracing, and fitting per-skill BKT parameters from real data - both need a corpus of real learner answers that does not exist yet.

requirements.title: Spaced repetition scheduling with adaptive intervals
requirements.notes: Intervals adapt to the individual learner's performance rather than a fixed calendar. Review items are labelled with why they appear (not_yet_mastered or due_for_review). Interleaving review questions into live practice sets is not yet done.

requirements.title: Intervention triggers for struggle and rapid mastery
requirements.notes: Server-side triggers during a practice session: three consecutive wrong answers suggests reviewing or taking a hint; more than ten minutes on one question suggests a hint; a flawless unaided run at the hardest tier suggests moving to the advanced track. Decided server-side so the client cannot suppress them, and surfaced in the practice UI.

requirements.title: Multi-track adaptation with separate core/advanced models
requirements.notes: Core and advanced now have separate adaptive models (check:multi-track-adaptation). Ability is held per (learner, track) in track_ability and each track's estimate is the prior for the next diagnostic started in that track, so what a learner has shown in core changes where core begins and leaves advanced untouched. Verified end to end over HTTP: the same learner reaching 2.11 in core after a perfect core diagnostic and -1.54 in advanced after an all-wrong one, starting at boss and practice respectively, with neither track moving on the other's evidence. One pooled estimate could not express that -- a strong core record would drag advanced up and drop the child into enrichment work above them, and a weak advanced record would drag core down and hand them practice they finished months ago; both failures are invisible in an average. Remembered confidence is deliberately widened (sd floor 0.8) so an old measurement informs where a new diagnostic starts without overruling what the learner does today. IRT's estimator now accepts a prior, which is what makes the carry-over possible.

requirements.title: Formative embedded questions with immediate feedback
Summative mastery checks and unit tests
requirements.notes: Chapter-level mastery checks and unit tests both implemented and verified (check:unit-tests). A unit test spans every authored topic in a unit, drawn equally from each and capped by the smallest bank so the score is not weighted by how many questions each topic happens to have; it is marked server-side, reports a per-topic breakdown naming the weakest topic, credits knowledge tracing per topic, and is stored in its own table so a unit key never appears where a topic id is expected. Units with fewer than two authored topics are refused by name rather than served as a mastery check under another label. Still open: AI-graded open-ended responses, which need the LLM provider account that 4.1.11 is blocked on — kept partial for that reason alone.

requirements.title: Feedback types incl. partial credit and elegance bonus
requirements.notes: Partial credit on multi-step answers: ordering earns credit for positions in the right place, select-all rewards correct picks and penalises wrong ones so guessing everything scores worse than a careful partial answer. Single-answer types stay all-or-nothing. An elegance bonus for creative solutions is not built - it would need judgement this cannot make honestly.

requirements.title: Three-level hints reducing star rating
Error analysis categorising common mistakes
requirements.notes: Wrong answers are classified into named misconceptions (sign error, reversed coordinates, place value, off by one, partial/over selection, reversed ordering, blank). Recorded per learner and reported by category and topic. Unrecognised mistakes are reported as unclassified rather than forced into a bucket.

requirements.title: Mastery thresholds configurable, default 90/80
requirements.notes: Defaults stay 90% core / 80% advanced and are enforced server-side. They are now configurable by an administrator at run time (check:configurable-mastery), stored rather than held in memory so a deploy cannot silently revert a school to 90% mid-term, and read through on every call so no process serves a stale value. Out-of-range values are refused rather than clamped -- an admin who typed 5 meant something, and quietly storing 50 would leave them believing the platform did what they asked -- with the accepted range published by the endpoint. Changing a threshold moves the live judgement of mastery (review queue, per-topic thresholds, curriculum payload) but never rewrites recorded results, so an admin cannot change what a child actually scored. Readable by any signed-in user, since the bar a learner is held to is not a secret from them; writable by admins only, and audited. Deliberately platform-wide, not per class: a learner can be in two classes, and per-class thresholds would make the same topic mastered and unmastered at once with no non-arbitrary precedence rule -- that needs a decision, not a column. Mastery decay is still not implemented.

requirements.title: Web authoring tools for all content types
requirements.notes: Content is authored as reviewed source modules with a validating linter and CI enforcement rather than a web editor. A browser-based authoring tool with templates and versioning is not built.

requirements.title: Asset management with tagging and licensing
Curriculum mapping to standards
requirements.notes: All 16 authored topics mapped to real Common Core State Standards codes, each checked against the actual CCSSM structure rather than guessed from the topic name. Deliberately does NOT map the other 312 topics - claiming standards alignment for content that does not exist would be worse than no mapping. Coverage grows as content is authored.

requirements.title: Localisation of text, audio and notation
QA workflow with preview and automated checks
requirements.notes: Content linter over every question, puzzle, proof and generator template, with each of its 13 rules proven to fire on deliberately broken content, plus preview-as-student and an approval workflow (check:content-review-workflow). The preview is built from the same publicQuestion() the learner endpoints use rather than a reviewer-specific rendering -- a separately assembled preview drifts, and a reviewer ends up approving a version no child is served; answers are shown to the reviewer separately and deliberately. Sign-off is bound to a hash of the exact content: reformatting the source keeps an approval, any change of meaning revokes it and the topic reports as stale naming the version that was actually approved. An approval recorded against a topic id alone would survive every later edit, so a bank approved in March would still read as approved after a June rewrite nobody checked -- worse than no approval, because it looks like assurance.

requirements.title: Clever/ClassLink/Google Classroom rostering and SSO
requirements.notes: Each requires a vendor developer account and approval the user must obtain.

requirements.title: REST API, webhooks, GraphQL
requirements.notes: REST API exists, and outbound webhooks are now built (check:webhooks): three events, HMAC-SHA256 signed with a per-subscription secret shown once and never listed back, verified constant-time, delivered after the response and never awaited so a school's slow endpoint cannot hold up a child mid-round, with every delivery outcome recorded so a broken integration is visible rather than discovered weeks later. The security work is the bulk of it: a webhook is a user-supplied URL the SERVER fetches, which unguarded is a request-forgery primitive pointed at loopback or at 169.254.169.254 for cloud credentials. Destinations are checked against their RESOLVED addresses -- a hostname proves nothing about where the packet goes -- and re-checked at send time, since DNS can be repointed after approval. GraphQL is NOT built: it needs a parser dependency, and this server deliberately runs on express and cookie-parser alone with everything else from the Node standard library. That is a dependency decision to take deliberately rather than one to slip in, so it is left open.

requirements.title: Data export CSV/PDF and FERPA-compliant student export
requirements.notes: CSV for learners and classes, printable report, and the full JSON account export from /api/me/export. CSV escaping verified against a name containing a comma and quotes; access control verified on every export.

requirements.title: Email and push notifications
requirements.notes: Needs SMTP/push provider credentials.

requirements.title: LTI 1.3 Advantage support
Performance: lesson load < 2s broadband, < 5s 3G
requirements.notes: Server-side latency measured on every endpoint a screen needs, all well inside budget, plus payload size and concurrency checks including that 10 simultaneous writes all record without corrupting the progress row. This measures the SERVER only: real page-load time over broadband or 3G depends on network and device and cannot be established from here.

requirements.title: Scalability to 50,000 concurrent users
requirements.notes: SQLite single-node will not meet this; needs Postgres and horizontal scaling.

requirements.title: Security and privacy: COPPA, FERPA, GDPR, encryption, RBAC, audit logs
requirements.notes: Done and verified: security headers incl. CSP, brute-force limiting on login, COPPA consent required at registration, audit log, FERPA/GDPR export and erasure, secure cookie in production, RBAC across parent, teacher and admin roles with admin not self-assignable, and -- new -- automated retention deletion (check:retention-deletion). Retention was previously prose on an admin endpoint that no code read; one POLICY object is now both rendered to admins and enforced by a sweep that runs daily by default, deleting expired sessions and reset tokens, audit entries past 400 days, and audit rows whose account is gone. Learner work is deliberately never swept on a timer -- it is retained while the learner exists and removed with them -- because deleting a year of a child's progress from a family that did nothing wrong is a worse failure than holding it. The check pins both directions at each boundary, that learner work survives, and that the sweep is idempotent, admin-only and audited. NOT done: encryption at rest (needs a deployment and KMS decision) and a third-party penetration test.

requirements.title: Reliability: 99.95% uptime, backups, offline degradation
requirements.notes: Consistent backups via VACUUM INTO, verified restorable and integrity-checked, now running on a schedule with bounded retention. Graceful shutdown drains in-flight requests. NOT done: uptime SLA, point-in-time recovery, multi-region failover, and a restore drill that rebuilds a running service from a snapshot.

requirements.title: Accessibility WCAG 2.1 AA incl. keyboard and screen reader
requirements.notes: axe-core over real rendered markup of 5 screens, zero WCAG 2.1 A/AA violations; 24 contrast pairs >= 4.5:1 in both themes; skip link, landmarks, live regions, non-colour correctness markers, labelled controls, visible focus.

requirements.title: Cross-platform web + native iOS/Android with offline sync
requirements.notes: Responsive web app with an offline shell, verified to build and emit every shell file. Native iOS and Android apps are not built, and offline PRACTICE (queuing answers while disconnected and syncing later) is not implemented - only the shell loads offline.

requirements.title: Usability: age-appropriate UI, onboarding, multilingual
requirements.notes: The interface scales with the grade being worked on: K-2 gets 60px touch targets, 18% larger type and warm orange; 3-5 teal; 6-8 a denser layout at the 48px minimum. Rounded display face, pill buttons, pressable card shadows, and monsters that react to answers - cheering, wincing or looking thoughtful. Celebration never carries meaning alone; correctness is always stated in words. All motion is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion, confetti included. NOT done: onboarding tutorial, contextual help, multilingual copy.

requirements.title: Localisation incl. RTL
Legal compliance incl. content licensing
requirements.notes: Legal review and contest-problem licensing are the user's decisions.

requirements.title: Web client with PWA capability
requirements.notes: Installable PWA: manifest, maskable icon, theme colour, and a service worker caching the app shell for offline opening. The API is deliberately never cached - a cached answer could be replayed against the grader and stale progress would be worse than an honest offline message. Registered only in production builds.

requirements.title: API gateway and microservices
requirements.notes: Single Express service with modular routes; not decomposed.

requirements.title: Postgres + NoSQL + Redis + Elasticsearch
requirements.notes: Currently SQLite only, deliberately, to avoid external accounts.

requirements.title: CDN and video streaming
requirements.notes: Static assets are served by the API process with cache headers. No CDN - that is a deployment decision that follows from choosing a host.

requirements.title: Analytics pipeline and AI services
requirements.notes: Depends on the AI provider decision.

requirements.title: OAuth2/OIDC, rate limiting, DDoS protection, KMS
CI/CD with automated tests and IaC
requirements.notes: CI runs the full requirement suite on every push and now also validates the infrastructure (terraform fmt -check and terraform validate, no credentials needed). Infrastructure as Code is done (check:infrastructure-as-code): infra/ declares the Fly app, the database volume and the machine in Terraform, where previously the only record of them was prose in DEPLOY.md and whatever someone typed once. The volume carries prevent_destroy because Fly replaces a volume when an immutable attribute changes and a replaced volume is an empty one -- a one-word region edit would otherwise plan the deletion of every learner's progress. machine_count is validated to 1: two machines cannot share one SQLite volume and would serve silently diverging databases. Backup interval and retention sweep are set in infrastructure rather than left to code defaults, and the check scans every file under infra/ for committed credentials. A single-container Dockerfile builds the client and serves it from the API, with Fly and Render configs pointing health checks at /ready and mounting persistent storage. NOT done: an actual deployment, which needs a host account. Blue-green releases are NOT possible in this architecture and the config says so rather than leaving it looking forgotten -- they need two live machines, and the single SQLite volume only one can mount; a networked database is the prerequisite, so releases are rolling with a health gate.

requirements.title: All K-8 core and advanced curriculum loaded and standards-aligned
requirements.notes: 1098 questions across 128 topics spanning K through grade 8, every one validated: at least 5 questions and 2 tiers per topic, explanations present, options unique, ordering answers permutations of their items, and every authored topic on the prerequisite graph. Every authored topic is also mapped to real CCSSM codes (check:standards-mapping). Grades 1 through 7's core curricula are all fully authored, and Kindergarten's core is authored except three topics with no real CCSSM standard (ordinal numbers, patterns, logic puzzles). 200 of 328 topics still have no content -- most K-8 advanced/enrichment topics remain unauthored, and Grade 8 has only 3 core topics authored so far (of 16).

requirements.title: Adaptive engine validated with 1,000 beta students per grade
requirements.notes: Requires real users; cannot be satisfied by code alone.

requirements.title: End-to-end flow: diagnostic to lesson to practice to mastery check to review
requirements.notes: Diagnostic -> practice -> review queue -> mastery check -> progress verified as one journey. The 'lesson' step of the spec's flow is not included: comic lessons (3.2.1) do not exist yet.

requirements.title: Competition mode and proof trainer operational
requirements.notes: Competition mode and proof trainer are both operational with sample content and verified end to end. Neither has the breadth of content the spec envisages.

requirements.title: AI tutor under 3s response with safety filters
Parent, teacher, admin dashboards showing accurate real-time data
requirements.notes: All three dashboards exist and are verified against real recorded work: parent progress, teacher class heatmap, and admin aggregate analytics. Each is access-controlled and shows only what that role should see.

requirements.title: Rostering and LTI integrations tested
WCAG 2.1 AA audit passes
requirements.notes: Automated AA audit passes on every screen built so far and runs in CI. A manual screen-reader pass (NVDA/VoiceOver) is still worth doing before release; automated tooling catches roughly half of WCAG issues.

requirements.title: Penetration testing shows no critical vulnerabilities
requirements.notes: Automated attack scan run in CI: SQL injection payloads against login, learner creation and topic-id URL paths; XSS against the one server-rendered HTML surface (the printable report) plus a source check that the React client never uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML; IDOR probes against four learner-scoped endpoints from an unrelated account; forged and empty session cookies; a parent account attempting to create a class without the teacher role; prototype pollution via a JSON body; path traversal against the static file server. Zero findings, and one real fix landed while writing it: an admin-analytics query used string-interpolated SQL rather than a parameterised one -- not currently exploitable since the interpolated value was server-generated, but exactly the pattern that becomes a real SQL injection the moment someone copies it with user input. This is explicitly NOT a substitute for professional penetration testing: it is a fixed, narrow set of automated attacks, not the open-ended probing a real pen tester would do.

requirements.title: Load testing confirms 50,000 concurrent users
requirements.notes: Modest concurrency verified (40 simultaneous reads, 10 simultaneous writes, no corruption). The spec's 50,000 concurrent users needs a load-testing rig and horizontal scaling; SQLite on a single node will not meet it.

requirements.title: Mobile apps approved on both stores with offline mode
requirements.notes: Requires paid developer accounts the user must hold.

requirements.title: Mock contest scored accurately with correct leaderboards
requirements.notes: Mock contests score accurately and timing is enforced, both verified, and contest leaderboards are now built (check:contest-leaderboard). Ranked on each learner's BEST attempt at a format -- ranking every attempt would put the child with the most free time on top rather than the one who did best, and would quietly reward re-sitting the same paper -- ordered by score then by time, because equal scores left unordered are not a result. Expired papers are excluded and members with no completed paper are reported as absent rather than implied to be last. It inherits the same safeguards as the points board rather than a looser set: off until a teacher enables it, anonymised unless they allow names, and scoped to one class. A contest board is the most tempting place to add a global ranking and the worst place to do it -- a child who has just been timed and scored is exactly the child who should not then be ranked against strangers.

requirements.title: Proof checker accurate for sample proofs at each grade
requirements.notes: Structural checking is accurate for every authored proof at each grade level, verified for both acceptance and rejection. This is not a general proof checker.

requirements.title: Answers never sent to the client; server grades
requirements.notes: Not in the spec explicitly, but required by 4.1.4 hints and assessment integrity.

requirements.title: Passwords stored hashed; sessions in httpOnly cookies
Learner data isolated between accounts
Progress durable across restarts
Schema migrations apply to existing databases
requirements.notes: Found the hard way: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS skips existing tables, so new columns never reached the dev database and every request 500'd. Migrations are now idempotent and a check boots against an old-schema file.

requirements.title: Account recoverable: password reset without data loss
requirements.notes: Reset tokens are stored only as a SHA-256 hash, single use, 30 minute expiry, and requesting one gives an identical response whether or not the account exists. Completing a reset revokes every existing session, so it locks out whoever prompted it. Learner and progress data survive intact. NOTE: with no email provider (9.4 blocked) the token is returned directly to the caller, which is rate limited but means anyone who can reach the endpoint for a known address can reset it. Set DELIVER_RESET_TOKEN=false once SMTP exists.

requirements.title: Graceful shutdown and error handling
requirements.notes: Express error handler returns JSON and never a stack trace; malformed and oversized bodies handled. SIGTERM drains in-flight requests and exits 0 within a 10s timeout, so a redeploy does not lose writes. uncaughtException logs and shuts down rather than serving from an unknown state.

requirements.title: Backups run on a schedule
requirements.notes: BACKUP_INTERVAL_HOURS runs backups on a timer with bounded retention, verified by running a server on a one-second interval and confirming snapshots appear, pruning holds, and the result passes an integrity check. Off by default so development does not litter the disk.
